segments.text: This is a brand new type of military aircraft from Andrew.
Its name is Thunder.
And the crazy part is that it can fly autonomously with no pilot and no cockpit.
Now, Thunder's job is like something straight out of Top Gun.
It flies right next to an Apache helicopter as its robotic wingman.
Think of it like the bodyguard flying shotgun, which takes the most dangerous job away so the crew doesn't have to.
But the coolest part about Thunder isn't that it flies autonomously, it's that it can fly in two different ways.
Thunder is what's called a tilt rail.
Which means the rotors can tilt forwards and backwards.
On takeoff, they point straight at the sky, so Thunder can lift off like a helicopter.
Then, once airborne, they tilt forward like propellers, so it can fly like a plane.
This single innovation is why Thunder can fly full speed with an Apache helicopter, while a normal drone would get left behind.
Now, there's one thing about Thunder's design that is super surprising.
Even though there's no pilot in the sky, it's also not being controlled manually by humans on the ground either.
This will sound like sci-fi, but there's actually no person in control of flying this thing.
A soldier gives Thunder a task, and then it figures out the route, the formation, and the timing.
So the military is going from flying aircraft to coaching them.
Now, the Apache helicopter has been the king of attack aviation since the 1980s.
And Andrew says one Apache flying with three thunders can carry three times more weapons into a fight, while the crew can stay out of the most dangerous airspace.
It's early, but this feels like the beginning of the autonomous military era.
Fall for more stories like this on tech, AI, and robotics.
